{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6",
    "line": 13,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "totalPages is off by one for groups with an exact multiple of limit",
    "body": "totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users with limit 50), this returns one extra page. The pagination controls then show page 1 of 2, leaving 'next' enabled. Clicking next sets offset to user_count, requests an empty page, and displays an empty last page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) and keep the zero-member special case."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/groups_controller.rb",
    "line": 22,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Public group member pages are silently truncated to 50 users",
    "body": "The members action now defaults limit to 50 and always applies limit/offset. The public route group-members.js.es6 calls model.findMembers() with the model's defaults (limit 50, offset 0), and the public group/members.hbs template has no pagination controls. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. As a result, any public group with more than 50 members will display only the first 50 with no way to reach the rest. Either add public pagination or preserve the old behavior for the public UI."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/groups_controller.rb",
    "line": 26,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "limit and offset are not validated or clamped",
    "body": "limit and offset are taken directly from query parameters with .to_i and passed to ActiveRecord's limit/offset. Negative values such as ?limit=-1 or ?offset=-1 can reach PostgreSQL, which rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET and causes a 500. Very large limit values also allow a client to force a large result set. These values should be validated, clamped to sane bounds, or both."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb",
    "line": 72,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Add members succeeds silently when usernames are not found",
    "body": "add_members looks up each username and silently skips users it cannot find, then returns success_json even if no members were added. The admin UI treats this as a successful Add operation, so a typo or whitespace after a comma can make the request report success while no user is added. The dedicated add-members endpoint should report unknown usernames or return validation errors instead of accepting them silently."
  },
  {
    "file": "spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb",
    "line": 115,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "remove_member spec uses PUT instead of DELETE",
    "body": "The route is defined as delete \"members\" => \"groups#remove_member\", but this spec uses xhr :put, :remove_member. Controller specs invoke the action directly rather than going through the router, so this test would pass even if the DELETE route were missing or misrouted. It should use xhr :delete, and ideally a request spec should cover the actual route and HTTP method."
  }

findings.title: totalPages is off by one for groups with an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users with limit 50), this returns one extra page. The pagination controls then show page 1 of 2, leaving 'next' enabled. Clicking next sets offset to user_count, requests an empty page, and displays an empty last page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) and keep the zero-member special case.

findings.title: Public group member pages are silently truncated to 50 users
findings.body: The members action now defaults limit to 50 and always applies limit/offset. The public route group-members.js.es6 calls model.findMembers() with the model's defaults (limit 50, offset 0), and the public group/members.hbs template has no pagination controls. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. As a result, any public group with more than 50 members will display only the first 50 with no way to reach the rest. Either add public pagination or preserve the old behavior for the public UI.

findings.title: limit and offset are not validated or clamped
findings.body: limit and offset are taken directly from query parameters with .to_i and passed to ActiveRecord's limit/offset. Negative values such as ?limit=-1 or ?offset=-1 can reach PostgreSQL, which rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET and causes a 500. Very large limit values also allow a client to force a large result set. These values should be validated, clamped to sane bounds, or both.

findings.title: Add members succeeds silently when usernames are not found
findings.body: add_members looks up each username and silently skips users it cannot find, then returns success_json even if no members were added. The admin UI treats this as a successful Add operation, so a typo or whitespace after a comma can make the request report success while no user is added. The dedicated add-members endpoint should report unknown usernames or return validation errors instead of accepting them silently.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT instead of DELETE
findings.body: The route is defined as delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", but this spec uses xhr :put, :remove_member. Controller specs invoke the action directly rather than going through the router, so this test would pass even if the DELETE route were missing or misrouted. It should use xhr :delete, and ideally a request spec should cover the actual route and HTTP method.
